housing: Kirklees covers Huddersfield, Dewsbury, Batley and the Spen Valley towns, and the Pennine valleys of the Colne and Holme. Much of the housing is Victorian stone terraces and back-to-backs built for the wool and textile mills, often on steep hillsides, with converted mills and student flats in Huddersfield near the university. The valleys have weavers' cottages and stone farmhouses, while the outskirts of the towns have interwar, post-war and modern estates. Rents rose sharply in the year to August 2026.
checkinTips: Stone terraces and back-to-backs: look for damp on thick walls, especially on walls built into the hillside, and photograph cellars and shared yards.
Steep hillside homes in Lockwood, Holmfirth and the valleys: photograph steps, sloping paths and retaining walls, and note any cracking.
Student shared houses near the University of Huddersfield: photograph each bedroom's lock and furniture, fire doors, alarms and the kitchen.
Converted mills and town-centre flats: note fob and key counts, lifts, bin stores and bike stores, and look for condensation around large windows.
Homes near the Colne, Holme and Calder: look for signs of past flooding or damp in ground-floor rooms.
Pennine homes at height: record the boiler, radiators, loft insulation and any frost damage to outside pipes, gutters or pointing.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Kirklees Council's private sector housing team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
